transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... I guess I'm here because of something at work. I teach preschool, and... well, the second I spot balloons at school, even if they're just across the hallway... my chest tightens. I just kind of freeze for a moment... before I can really think clearly about what I’m supposed to be doing.
Have balloons ever been involved in a particularly upsetting or frightening experience for you?
Um... no. Not really. I don't remember anything like that happening. I just... I've just never liked them.
Does your reaction to balloons happen only at work or does it also occur in other situations or places?
Um... it's not just at work. I guess... it happens anywhere they are. I just... I try not to be around them.
When you see balloons and your chest tightens, what is going through your mind in that moment?

Um... I don't know. I guess... I know they're just decorations. But when I see one... especially if it looks stretched really tight, or it's bobbing around near the kids... I just keep thinking it's going to burst right in my face. I... I know I get way more scared than I should for something like that. It's just... yeah.
Is the thought of the balloon bursting what scares you, or is it something else about the balloon itself?
Um... I'm not really sure. I think... it's mostly just the thought of it popping. I don't really know if it's... anything else about them. I just don't like them.
Does your fear of balloons interfere with your daily activities or social relationships outside of work?

Um... I guess outside of work I just avoid them. But... it has started affecting my job. I've had to... let the aides take over for the normal classroom celebrations. And... recently I missed helping with this festival art table I had planned, because of it. My supervisor noticed... so, yeah. It's... it's getting in the way.
Have you been avoiding places or events where you think balloons might be present?

Um... yeah, I guess so. Like I mentioned, I've been... having the aides handle the birthday circles. And just moving away from the festival tables if they're around. If I absolutely have to stay in the room... I just keep my distance. I try not to look at them... and just focus on getting through it.
Are there any situations where you feel forced to confront balloons and can't avoid them?
Um... no, not really. I usually just... find an excuse to leave the room. Or, like I said, I just stay in the back. I don't think I've ever been totally trapped where I couldn't get away from them.
How would you rate your level of anxiety when you're in a situation where you can't avoid balloons?

Um... I'm not really sure. Like I said, I always just... find a way out of it. So I haven't really been stuck where I absolutely couldn't leave. I don't really know how to rate it... it's just bad enough that I make sure I get away.
Is your fear specifically of the balloon bursting, or is it also the appearance or presence of the balloon itself that scares you?

Um... it's mostly the bursting. I mean, I know it's just a decoration for the kids, but... when I see one that looks really stretched out, or it's just sort of bobbing around near the children... it just feels like it's going to pop right in my face. It just... scares me more than it probably should.
Is the fear of the balloon bursting because of the loud noise it would make, or is it more about the balloon actually popping?
Um... I guess I'm not totally sure. I just... I don't like the popping. The noise is bad, but just... the whole thing. I don't know, it's just the popping.
Is the noise of the balloon popping the main thing that scares you, or is it more the act of the balloon actually bursting?
Um... I really don't know. It's... kind of hard to separate the two. I just don't like when they pop. I haven't really thought about which part of it is worse.
Is the loud noise of the balloon popping the main thing that scares you?
Um... I don't think it's just the noise. I... I really don't know how else to explain it. Like I said, I'm just not sure. I just don't like it.
Is the fear of the balloon bursting more about what you see happening or what you hear when it pops?
I... I honestly couldn't tell you. It's just the whole thing happening at once. I don't really break it down like that... it's just the popping.
Is the fear you experience when you think about a balloon bursting more related to the sound it makes or the sight of it popping!
I... I really don't know. Like I said, it's just the whole thing. I haven't really thought about if it's the sound or the sight. It's just... it popping.
When you imagine a balloon bursting, is it the picture in your mind of it popping that scares you or something else?
I just... I really don't know how to answer that. It's just the whole idea of it popping. I don't really picture it or... or focus on one part of it. It just scares me.
Is it the sound of the balloon bursting that scares you the most?
I don't know... I'm sorry, I just... I can't really separate it out like that. It's just the popping. That's all I can really say.
Is the fear you experience when you think about a balloon bursting more about the act of it bursting or something related to the consequences of it bursting?
I just... I really can't explain it any better. It's just the popping. I don't know about consequences or... or the act of it. It's just the whole thing. I don't know.
Is the noise of the balloon popping necessary for you to feel scared?
I'm not sure. I mean... they always make a noise when they pop, so I haven't really thought about it without the sound. I just... I really don't know.
Would you still be scared if a balloon were to burst silently?
I... I don't know. It's hard to imagine that. They just... they always make a sound. I can't really picture it without the noise.
